title: Investigate customer-reported token throughput collapse in private regions; implement prefetch circuit-breaker and int8 fallback
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Multiple customers running private deployments in eu-west-2 reported sudden token/sec collapses and increased TTFT starting 2026-03-09 after runtime release runtime-1.18. Impact: several production endpoints saw tokens/sec drop by ~60% for long-context requests and first-token lag increased 3-5x. Affected workloads are heterogeneous (mixed short and long context) and heavy KV-prefetch usage. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigation (hotfix), and a staged rollout of a lightweight fallback path to restore throughput while we complete a deeper kernel scheduler and router weight fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy model variant rwd/llama-2-70b-q5 in a private-hosted cluster in eu-west-2 with runtime-1.18
2) Replay mixed-length traffic (50% < 256 tokens, 50% ~3k tokens) using the customer trace linked below
3) Observe KV prefetch burst followed by queue explosion on multiplex router and kernel preemption logs in worker-stdout
4) Measure tokens/sec and TTFT from /metrics and compare to baseline from runtime-1.17
observed_metrics: tokens_per_second: dropped from ~2.4k to ~900 across affected pools
worker_cpu: 15% increase in context-switches and 30% increase in kernel preempt events
kv-prefetch-rate: 4x increase in miss-triggered prefetches leading to eviction churn
hypotheses: 1) Kernel scheduler heuristic change in runtime-1.18 causes inefficient preemption when context windows are heterogeneous
2) Router priority decay combined with KV prefetch aggressiveness creates transient concentrated load on a subset of workers, thrashing cache
3) Memory/quant lookup path introduced in 1.18 amplifies latency for int8 quantized kernels under eviction pressure
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Emergency call with customer and on-call SRE (Maya). Decided to implement a short circuit that disables KV prefetch for tenants showing >20% TTFT regression and to enable a lightweight int8-compatible model fallback for immediate throughput recovery.

2026-03-11: Engineering design review. Agreed on two parallel tracks: hotpatch A (config flag + circuit-breaker) and hotpatch B (int8 minimal-precision fallback variant). Both to be gated by canary policy and feature flags per-tenant.

2026-03-12: Security sync — fallback model uses existing signed artifacts; no new keying required. Security review marked required for on-prem rollout; approved as expedited (security_review_required: true).
2026-03-13: Canary started in eu-west-2 dedicated pool for 5% of traffic; initial metrics show tokens/sec recovery to ~85% baseline for canary tenants.
Next: prepare a rollback plan and a longer-term scheduler fix (ENG-142432 placeholder created).
